mirrorOrOtherProjectWarning: SEMI-DETACHED PAIR: every drawing and render shows TWO mirrored units joined at a party wall; this reference describes the WHOLE pair as drawn (one unit = one half, 6.96 m wide; halve the symmetric counts for a single unit). FRAME WARNING: the two entrance doors do NOT face the street - each sits in the side wall of the link between the main body and the projecting garage block (left unit's door faces LEFT, right unit's door faces RIGHT). FRONT here = the street side with the two garage doors, which the publisher labels as the front elevation (image 031) and where the plan's entry arrows point. No pictures of other projects.

uncertain: The schema's entrance fields cannot express this house with one enum value: there are two entrance doors, facing opposite side directions. If a single value is required use facade FRONT-approach / position LEFT for the left unit and RIGHT for the right unit. Because of this, FRONT (street side) shows NO entrance door; the doors are counted on LEFT and RIGHT.

If a consumer instead defines FRONT strictly as the wall plane containing the entrance door, then for a single unit the front would be that unit's outer side elevation (images 030 / 029) - the opposite reading to the publisher's labels.

FRONT storey 0: one ground-floor room window on the exposed main-body wall at each end, two single garage doors in the central timber-clad block. FRONT storey 1 (main body, above/behind the roof terrace): at each end a small narrow window, then a three-part glazed door set (~2.1-2.3 m wide, under the ~2.5 m threshold) opening onto the roof terrace.
REAR storey 0: four floor-to-ceiling glazed terrace doors (outer ones three-part ~1.9 m, inner ones two-part ~1.4 m). REAR storey 1: outer two-sash windows, inner glazed doors with French balconies.

LEFT facade, seen from outside left (rear) to right (front): two ground-floor windows on the white gable wall joined by a timber panel (two-sash dining window + narrow kitchen window; counted as 2), entrance door with a narrow glazed side strip in the timber-clad link, two horizontal strip windows in the garage side wall. LEFT storey 1: one narrow window in the gable wall. RIGHT is the exact mirror (listed front to rear as seen from outside: 2 garage strip windows, entrance door, narrow window, two-sash window).

Entrance doors stand in the re-entrant corner between main body and garage block with open steps in front; no canopy is visible in the render or elevations, so recessedOrPorch is given as false. The plan shows a dashed outline over the landing that might be a small overhang.

Per single unit (half): width 6.96 m; FRONT 0: WINDOW + GARAGE_DOOR, FRONT 1: WINDOW + GLAZED_DOOR; REAR 0: 2 GLAZED_DOOR, REAR 1: WINDOW + GLAZED_DOOR; outer side: storey 0 = 5 (2 windows, entrance door, 2 garage windows), storey 1 = 1; the other side is the party wall with no openings.

The site/roof plan shows a two-part rectangle on the rear roof plane of each unit (possibly solar collectors or roof hatches); nothing corresponding is drawn on the rear elevation, so no rooflights are counted.
Roof pitch 30 deg is the published value; height 8.91 m is read from the section (above floor level, not above terrain).
confidence: MEDIUM - geometry and counts are well documented (four elevations, plans, section, site plan, renders), but the building is a mirrored semi-detached pair with side-facing entrances, so the FRONT frame and 'the house' (pair vs. one unit) are open to interpretation.
